testingFeedback: 26 unique defects were found across automated tests, visual checks and contract/state review; all were fixed. Repeated assertions of one cause are counted once.
Five were critical: native movement state and event identity on restoration, cropped phone controls, incorrect Hub deadline/instruction metadata, and a hidden host RAF freezing its shared world.
Normal-input full expeditions on every route, including packet-loss and hidden-authority co-op, combined with deterministic mid-jump/mid-ladder snapshot continuation.
Syntax-only checks: useful for packaging, but unable to establish movement, progression, networking or presentation.
engineFeedback: Native Platformer traversal and posed Humanoid rigs supplied responsive movement and readable continuous animation, with useful native shape, weapon and hat hooks.
Yes. Map rows are top-first but cells are bottom-first; Platformer construction resets private movement timers; fixed-resolution screen scaling initially cropped narrow viewports.
The deterministic supply director, rock collisions, tool/key economy, extraction encounters and authoritative Hub shared-world adapter.
Keeping ladder topology, one-way floor contacts, animation and serialized native movement consistent across a renderer-free authority and visible clients.

Patched Screen.resize to permit fractional scaling when the viewport is smaller than the logical buffer. Game adapters also preserve native movement internals and ladder-crossing one-way ledges; the pristine engine baseline remains vendored.
Add native Platformer snapshot/restore with private movement timers, plus a fixed-resolution small-viewport regression case.
promptFeedback: The director plan specifies the complete action/resource loop, failure paths, accessibility and concrete proof to deliver.
Standalone internet play versus Hub integration was ambiguous. Followed the plan: standalone solo/local co-op, and online shared-world co-op through AI Hub.
Integrating one deterministic expedition across keyboard, pad, multitouch assists, attract play, couch ownership and a hidden online authority.

Use a shorter prioritized acceptance list and distinguish desired pacing from hard functional gates. Skilled scripted runs here take roughly two minutes; a ten-to-twelve-minute first success was not measured.

aiHub.name: Pickaxe Puddles
aiHub.description: Chop for gold, ricochet ore into ore, and race a rising key through three unruly mine chambers. A broken pick is only the beginning: go solo or share the payday with a partner.
aiHub.controls: Move A/D or arrows; W/S climb/duck; Space jump; J/left click chop; Q/right click redirect; E interact; Escape pause. Standard gamepad and touch supported.
